name: ClassPredictor
title: ClassPredictor: Academic Risk & Prerequisite Graphs | Parth Goyal
summary: I built ClassPredictor to map gaps in school foundations to the topics that depend on them, giving students a clearer starting point for preparation.
description: Explore Parth Goyal’s ClassPredictor: a React app that maps prerequisite dependencies, identifies academic bottlenecks, and prioritizes preparation.
problem: A weak foundation can make a later topic difficult even when a student is putting in time. A single score does not explain which prerequisite to revisit or where to begin.
approach: I modelled the relationship between foundational topics and the topics that depend on them. ClassPredictor uses those relationships to identify bottlenecks and turn a broad preparation problem into a set of priorities.

implementation.title: Map the dependencies
implementation.text: A directed prerequisite graph connects school foundations to later topics. The public project documentation describes a D3.js visualization that makes those connections visible.

implementation.title: Prioritize preparation
implementation.text: The risk engine considers prerequisite strength and the target exam. A prioritization matrix and phased roadmap help students decide what to work on first.

implementation.title: Ship a usable web app
implementation.text: I built the interface with React and Vite, with Firebase Firestore for telemetry and feedback. The source is public, so the implementation can be inspected alongside the demo.

contribution: I built and shipped ClassPredictor independently, including the interface, dependency-based prediction logic, and Firebase integration.
outcome: The portfolio’s original launch figures are 100+ organic users, with the first 100 reached in two days and ₹0 spent on marketing. These are my reported launch figures; the public repository documents the implementation.
note: The output is a planning aid based on the supplied inputs and prerequisite model. It is not a guarantee of an exam result.

name: SYNAPSE
title: SYNAPSE: AI Habit Support App | Parth Goyal
summary: I built SYNAPSE around a five-step reflection flow, personalized AI plans, daily check-ins, and support for getting back on track after a setback.
description: See how Parth Goyal built SYNAPSE with React, Firebase, Groq, and LLaMA: reflection flows, AI plans, daily check-ins, and streak tracking.
problem: A habit tracker can count days without helping someone understand the pattern behind a repeated behavior. I wanted to connect reflection, a concrete plan, and the next daily action.
approach: I built a five-step flow to collect the user’s pattern, then use an AI response to turn it into a personalized plan. Daily check-ins, streak logic, milestone drops, and setback responses keep that plan connected to ongoing use.

implementation.title: Turn reflection into context
implementation.text: The onboarding flow collects the pattern in five steps before requesting a plan. This gives the AI response context from the user’s own answers.

implementation.title: Verify requests on the server
implementation.text: Firebase Auth identifies the user. Server-side verification sits between the client and the AI request, rather than relying on a claim sent by the browser.

implementation.title: Support returning users
implementation.text: Firestore, check-ins, streak resets, notifications, and milestone logic support the ongoing experience. The app uses Groq with LLaMA 3.3 70B and is deployed with Vercel serverless functions.

contribution: I built the reflection flow, AI integration, authenticated request path, and the check-in and streak experience.
outcome: SYNAPSE is live. The public app demonstrates the experience; this portfolio does not report measured health outcomes or clinical validation.
note: SYNAPSE is a habit-support project. AI-generated plans are not medical advice or a substitute for professional care.

name: Verdikt
title: Verdikt: AI Market News Pipeline | Parth Goyal
summary: I built Verdikt to collect Indian market news, remove repeated stories, and organize Gemini-generated impact assessments in a multilingual terminal.
description: Explore Parth Goyal’s Verdikt: RSS ingestion, SHA-256 deduplication, Gemini impact scoring, and an English, Hindi, and Hinglish market news terminal.
problem: Market stories arrive across multiple publishers, often repeating the same development. Reading every feed separately makes it harder to identify what changed and which stories deserve attention.
approach: I separated continuous ingestion from the reading interface. The backend collects RSS items, deduplicates stories, and sends them through a Gemini-powered evaluation pipeline before the terminal presents the results.

implementation.title: Ingest across publishers
implementation.text: The pipeline collects RSS feeds from Moneycontrol, LiveMint, Economic Times, Hindu BusinessLine, and Zee Business, covering Indian market and policy developments.

implementation.title: Deduplicate and evaluate
implementation.text: SHA-256 hashing identifies repeated stories. A Gemini multi-agent evaluation pipeline assigns market-impact scores and categories; API key rotation supports continued processing.

implementation.title: Separate processing from delivery
implementation.text: The ingestion backend runs on Railway and the frontend on Vercel. React and Node.js are paired with Supabase, while the terminal supports English, Hindi, and Hinglish.

contribution: I built the news ingestion and evaluation pipeline and the multilingual terminal, connecting the continuously running backend to the frontend.
outcome: Verdikt is live with five news sources and three reading languages described in the project. No independently measured accuracy or uptime figure is claimed here.
note: Impact scores are AI-generated interpretations of news. They are not verified predictions or investment recommendations.
